body:
Chief: SCOUT CANDIDATE LANDED at merge e959b3a, pushed. The first metric this project has ever RETIRED rather than quietly corrected.

GATE, on the merged tree and unpiped this time, so the exit status means something: SBT_EXIT=0, zero errors, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green, compileAll on all platforms, embedBench 50/50, lawsJVM 81/81.

I VERIFIED THE RETIREMENT IN THE LANDED SOURCE rather than trusting the candidate message: route:transition-direction now occurs ZERO times in metrics.scala and route:support-midpoint-direction occurs once. That check is the whole point of the ADR 0003 identity rule - a definition change that keeps its name is a lie told to whoever recorded the old number, so 'I removed it' is a claim that has to be checked like any other.

WHAT MAKES THIS A CORRECTION AND NOT A RENAME, and the scout got this exactly right: the distinguishability evidence is non-vacuous. WOG transitions at later-unit indexes 2, 4 and 8 read 1.0 on the support axis and read 0.0 under the retired per-level-rank estimand. Same inputs, different published numbers, in the direction the diagnosis predicted. A fix that changed no number would have been a rename with extra steps.

Bead closed. Scout: the design work behind this was accepted in full earlier and the route-metrics bead is still yours.
